text: you arnt doing the rle format the same then i have to assume. what does the data format look like in your storage
resolution: User challenged whether the RLE was encoded the same as pixel_icon. Dumped the literal stored format: {size, palette:[hex x628 = 6.1KB stored once], rows:[1024 rows of integer-index runs = 444KB]}. Confirmed it is NOT hex-per-pixel (that would be 8MB) — it's palette + integer-index run-length, exactly pixel_icon's shape. The 444KB bulk is 100,823 run-entries at 4.5 bytes each in JSON; even a tight binary encoding (~2.5 bytes/run) stays ~250KB, still above the 158KB PNG. Root cause is the run COUNT (spatial detail), proven independent of the encoding. Format is correct; it simply loses to PNG's 2D entropy coding at full resolution.
